text:
Maria Gonzales: Quick thread — thinking about simplifying multi-region ownership by assigning tenants to small "ownership buckets" per region instead of a strict tenant->single-region mapping. Each bucket has a residency tag and a small list of allowed failover regions. Pros: fewer routing entries, easier rebalancing. Cons: more indirection. Thoughts? :thinking:
Devin Patel: curious — how does this work with strict data residency? if a tenant requires EU-only, can a bucket span EU+US?
Maria Gonzales: good Q. model is: bucket has a primary region (satisfies residency), plus optional read/compute replicas in other regions for latency. For strict residency, failover is either to other EU regions or blocked. We tag buckets with consent/residency flags.
Sophie Li: main ops concern: what happens to writes during bucket move/rehash? need a safe way to avoid split-writes. propose lease-based ownership: a short-lived lease token held by the primary region, includes: bucket_id, owner_region, lease_expiry. proxies attach `X-Tenant-Bucket` + `X-Bucket-Lease` on writes. Example header: `X-Tenant-Bucket: bkt-42; X-Bucket-Lease: owner=eu-west-1;exp=1710000000`
Paul Kramer: love the lease idea. also want run-time metrics: `bucket_move_duration_ms`, `inflight_writes_during_move`, `fallback_count_by_reason`. SLO: <1% requests hit fallback path in steady state.
deploy-bot: Canary started for `bucket-swap-controller v2` on cluster eu-west-1 — 20 buckets. Logs: https://deploys.internal/redwood/1234 :rocket:
Maria Gonzales: operational flow I imagine: 1) create target buckets mapping; 2) pre-warm caches in target region; 3) acquire lease on new owner; 4) drain inflight in old owner; 5) swap lease; 6) monitor metrics; rollback if error. Keep each step idempotent.
Devin Patel: for correctness: during swap there will be a short window where proxies could route to either. We need a single source of truth for routing — either central control-plane flip or RB update pushed via control-plane + push notifications to edge proxies. Any preference?
Sophie Li: prefer push via control-plane with immediate proxy ack. Fallback safety: proxies must reject writes unless they see a valid lease for their region OR a `X-Region-Fallback: allow` header from the control-plane. Fallback header should only be granted for tenants without strict residency. Pseudo-policy:
```
if tenant.residency == 'strict' and not owner_region in eu_regions:
  reject_write()
elif has_valid_lease():
  accept_write()
elif control_plane.allows_fallback(tenant):
  accept_with_retries()
else:
  fail_fast()
```
Paul Kramer: also think about data plane semantics on fallback: if we accept write in fallback region, we need a deterministic conflict-resolution plan. Last-write-wins is easy but risky for user-visible data. Alternatives: logical clocks + merge jobs, or queueing writes to primary with ack semantics. Tradeoffs: availability vs strong ordering.
Maria Gonzales: agree. propose default: allow fallback only for idempotent/non-critical endpoints (embeddings, inference), block for critical state writes. We'll tag API routes with `consistency_level` (strong/eventual) and enforce per-route fallback policy.
Devin Patel: what about cost/replication blowup when many tenants fallback to global pool during a region outage? need burst capacity plan + prioritized backpressure. Suggest a token-bucket per-region plus global emergency quota for enterprise customers.
Sophie Li: another operational quirk: prefix/KV caches. when fallback occurs we should avoid stale prefix cache in fallback region — we should force prefix cache invalidation on lease swap or set short prefix TTL for fallback-eligible buckets.
Paul Kramer: legal note: for EU-only tenants, fallback must be audited and attach reason codes in logs and tenant audit trail. add a `residency_fallback` event with fields: bucket_id, from_region, to_region, reason, operator_action.
Maria Gonzales: ok action items:
- Sophie: prototype lease header + proxy check (PR + small sim) — target EOW.
- Devin: work up routing control-plane flip vs push-notify trade doc and simulation plan.
- Paul: enumerate metrics + SLOs + audit events for RFC.
I'll draft short RFC next week that wires these pieces together. Anyone want to co-author? :eyes:
Devin Patel: happy to co-author. :+1:
Sophie Li: I'll own the prototype.
Paul Kramer: I'll review metrics + legal hooks.
Maria Gonzales: thanks all. leaving the canary running for a bit — will post results and a short writeup. :shipit:
